Hi everyone, this is Marcos from IT, with the new downtime protocol. After last month's incident, we had to make some changes. From now on, the backup server has to be in our second building, not in the same room. Every team has to do a one-hour drill, in March and in September. During the drill, you have to use the paper forms, like on the night of the crash. You don't have to print anything: the forms are already at every nurses' station. New staff have to do the training in their first month. It is required, and it takes only forty minutes. One lesson we learned is simple: nobody can prevent every problem, but a good plan prevents the panic. Thank you, and see you at the drill.

Let me tell you about my first mistake at work. It was my first week at a small hospital in Boston, more than twenty years ago. I sent a patient report to the wrong doctor. When I noticed it, I felt terrible, and I was afraid to tell my manager. But I told her, and she was not angry. She said: You don't have to hide a mistake. You have to tell me fast. Then we had to call the other doctor, and we fixed the problem in ten minutes. After that day, the whole team had to use a checklist before they sent any report. That checklist is still there today. For me, that is the best lesson learned: a mistake is information. If you say it early, the team can learn from it.
